title: The constant-index torsion bound IS the F20 lane with index t=(q-1)/d as the exact divisor that kills the sqrt-saving
reduced_to: Whether B = max_{b!=0} ||eta_b|| beats sqrt(q) per-frequency on thin dyadic mu_n (n=2^mu proper, q~n^beta) -- i.e. the BGK sqrt-cancellation among the m=(q-1)/n Gauss-sum phases, which the triangle inequality in the completion identity discards. This is the unchanged open core.
wall: W-BGK (square-root cancellation among the m=(q-1)/n Gauss periods / Paley eigenvalue spectrum)
evidence: Probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C039_constindex_saving.py (exact subgroup build via primitive_root, eta_b in high-precision complex, proper dyadic mu_n at large primes q=1 mod n, q~n^{3-4}). PART A (the connection's algebra) VERIFIED: dividing the in-tree-PROVEN inequality mul_norm_eta_torsion_le (t*||eta_b|| <= (t-1)sqrt(q)+1, SubgroupGaussSumWorstCase.lean) by t=(q-1)/d gives ||eta_b|| <= sqrt(q) - (sqrt(q)-1)/t; the probe confirms B <= this completion bound at every tested prime (n=8 q=1777; n=16 q=12433,65537; n=32 q=65537,262337; n=64 q=262337,1383553). The 'saving' (sqrt(q)-1)/t is exactly the +1/t trivial-character term and -> 0 as t=m grows (numerically 0.054-0.185 here), so the completion bound collapses to bare sqrt(q) at the prize (t=m~2^128) -- this CORRECTLY reproduces BurgessIndexOvershoot's sqrt(m/log m) overshoot. PART B REFUTES the central novel claim ('the ENTIRE F20 sqrt-cancellation lives in the single +1'): the TRUE saving over sqrt(q), realGap = completionBound - B_true, is 188x to 21000x larger than (sqrt(q)-1)/t and GROWS with q (n=8:188x, n=16:698x->3889x, n=64:3892x->21077x), while B_true/sqrt(n*log2 m) ~ 1.0 (0.91-1.34) confirms the true law is off the wall. The real sqrt-cancellation lives entirely in the DISCARDED triangle-inequality step ||sum_j tau_j|| <= sum_j ||tau_j|| of the completion identity, NOT in the trivial-character +1 term; the cofactor t governs only a negligible bookkeeping artifact, not the cancellation.
honest_note: PROVEN piece: the constant-index rearrangement ||eta_b|| <= sqrt(q)-(sqrt(q)-1)/t is a genuine one-line algebra consequence of an axiom-clean in-tree theorem, and the t->m collapse to bare sqrt(q) at the prize is correct (it re-derives BurgessIndexOvershoot). NOT shown / REFUTED: the connection's load-bearing assertion that this +1/t saving IS the F20 sqrt-cancellation -- it is not; the cancellation is thrown away by the triangle inequality before t ever enters, so the constant-index lane provides ZERO progress on beating sqrt(q). The lane is 'proven when t is small' precisely because then the COMPLEMENTARY subgroup is the small one (full-group QR/Paley case = the #400 trap, not the prize). At the prize both d=n and t=m exceed n, so neither completion is constant-index AND the saving is negligible -- the open core (W-BGK) is untouched. No Lean attempted: the algebra is a trivial corollary, the substantive part is the refutation of the cancellation-attribution, which the probe settles. No closure.
